land.text: the Sanjak of Trikala (granted to Ali in 1787) and the Ioannina post: infobox "Preceded by Ioannina Eyalet and Pashalik of Berat"

predecessors.note: Ali was granted the Sanjak of Trikala in 1787 and is first called Pasha of Ioannina on 15 March 1788.

land.text: the pashalik's land after Ali's death, infobox "Succeeded by Ioannina Eyalet"

successors.note: Ottoman direct rule; the Greek Revolution of 1821 had already begun in the south.

capitals.name: Yanina (Ioannina)
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Yanina (Ioannina). Tepelenë was Ali's birthplace and seat before.

rulers.name: Ali Pasha of Tepelenë (Ali Pasha of Ioannina)
rulers.title: pasha
rulers.note: Infobox 1787-1822; killed 24 January 1822. Sons Veli (Pasha of Trikala from 1787, Pasha of the Morea 1807-1812) and Muhtar governed parts.

correction.text: the Sanjak of Trikala (Thessaly), taken in 1787, and the Ioannina post Ali seized in 1787 or 1788

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row. "1787: Took the Sanjak of Trikala and delegated its pashaship to son Veli"; "1787 or 1788: Seized Ioannina ... This marked the beginning of the Pashalik of Yanina". Radius round Ioannina is the researcher's reading of the sanjak.

correction.text: Ioannina, Thessaly, and the 1789-1791 gains: Konitsa, Libohovë, Përmet and Tepelenë (from Avlona), and Arta on the Gulf of Arta

keyframe_review.note: "1789-1791: Konitsa; Libohovë, Përmet, and Tepelenë (from Avlona); Arta, giving access to the Ionian Sea via the Gulf of Arta". Konitsa and Libohovë fall inside the radii.

correction.text: the same, with control reaching "down to Livadia and the Gulf of Corinth" through Muhtar's appointments

keyframe_review.note: Ali page: in 1792 Muhtar's appointments "stretch[ed] for the first time Ali's control down to Livadia and the Gulf of Corinth". Control by appointment, so confidence 2 for the land; Central Greece (Stereá Elláda) is the researcher's reading of Livadia and the gulf shore.

correction.text: the Ionian coast: Butrint, Igoumenitsa, Preveza and Vonitsa taken from the French in 1798, and Himara annexed in 1799 "extending Ali's control along the coast to Vlorë"

keyframe_review.note: "1798: Seized Butrint, Igoumenitsa, Preveza, and Vonitsa from the French. Parga stayed French"; "Himara was later annexed in 1799". Epirus (Ipeiros) stands for the coast strip; Parga is inside it but stayed French until 1819, a small error on the cell grid.

correction.text: Delvinë, taken in 1802 "after seven years of conflict", giving "Epirus from Arta to Tepelenë and Vlorë", and Souli, conquered in 1803

keyframe_review.note: Ali page: 1802 Delvinë; 1803 Souli. The Yanina page puts Delvina's reconquest and the annexation of Gjirokastër in 1811, so Gjirokastër is left out here.

correction.text: Karli-Eli (Aetolia-Acarnania), annexed in 1806 after Mihrişah Valide Sultan's death in 1805

keyframe_review.note: "Karli-Eli taken after Mihrişah's death in 1805"; Dytiki Ellada stands for Karli-Eli and is wider than it.

correction.text: the Morea (Peloponnese), ruled by Veli 1807-1812 and "incorporated"

keyframe_review.note: "1807-1812: Veli ruled Morea (Peloponnese), which was incorporated." Ali page: Veli became Pasha of the Morea Eyalet in 1807.

correction.text: Berat, invaded in 1809 and passed to Muhtar as a dowry

keyframe_review.note: "1809: Invaded Berat; its territories passed to Muhtar as a dowry." The Ali page says the siege of Berat is undated (1809-1810).

correction.text: the rest of the Sanjak of Avlona (Vlorë), seized in 1810 after Sephir Bey's assassination

keyframe_review.note: "1810: Seized the remainder of the Sanjak of Avlona after Sephir Bey's assassination."

correction.text: Delvina reconquered and Gjirokastër annexed in 1811; by 1811 "the sanjaks of Ohrid, Elbasan, Gjirokastër and Delvinë were incorporated"

keyframe_review.note: Yanina page: "1811: Reconquered Delvina and annexed Gjirokastër"; Ali page for Ohrid and Elbasan (the Yanina page is silent on their dates).

correction.text: the peak pashalik without the Morea, which Veli left in 1812

keyframe_review.note: "Veli ruled Morea 1807-1812". The Yanina page's peak list for 1822 still names the Morea, Elbasan, Ohrid and Görice (Korçë), a cumulative list: this keyframe drops the Morea after 1812 because no page dates a return, and leaves Korçë out as undated. Infobox footnote (Papageorgiou 2014): "covered an area of 75,000 sq km"; the 1812-1822 keyframe is about 52,000 km2 on the cell grid (ratio 0.7; 67,500 km2 with the Morea in 1807-1811), within the factor of two. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: split at 1820, when Berat passes to the Pashalik of Scutari]

correction.text: the peak pashalik without the Morea, which Veli left in 1812; without Berat, which the Mustafa Pasha Bushati page says "was appropriated to him" in 1820

keyframe_review.note: 1820: "In 1820, the sanjak of Berat was appropriated to him" (Mustafa Pasha Bushati page), and the Ali page has Ali declared a rebel in 1820; the Pashalik of Scutari dossier carries the matching gain. The rest of the 1812-1822 shape is unchanged (peak area about 52,000 km2 against the 75,000 km2 of the infobox footnote, ratio 0.7). [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: new keyframe, 5 cells fewer]

region.text: the Sanjak of Trikala (Thessaly) and Ioannina

ledger.note: 1787: Ali Pasha takes the Sanjak of Trikala and, in 1787 or 1788, seizes Ioannina: "This marked the beginning of the Pashalik of Yanina." The Ali page: "Ali was granted the Sanjak of Tirhala in 1787"; first called Pasha of Ioannina on 15 March 1788.

region.text: Souli, in the Thesprotia mountains: first invasion in 1789

ledger.note: 1789: Ali's first invasion of Souli; further campaigns in 1790, 1792, 1800 and 1802 (the Yanina page also links the war as 1789-1793). A peace in 1792 returned captured villages.

region.text: Konitsa, Libohovë, Përmet and Tepelenë (from Avlona), and Arta, over 1789-1791

ledger.note: 1789-1791: Ali takes Konitsa, Libohovë, Përmet and Tepelenë "from Avlona" and Arta, "giving access to the Ionian Sea via the Gulf of Arta". One event at the end of the span.

region.text: central Greece "down to Livadia and the Gulf of Corinth", control by Muhtar's appointments

ledger.note: 1792: Muhtar's appointments "stretch[ed] for the first time Ali's control down to Livadia and the Gulf of Corinth".

region.text: Butrint, Igoumenitsa, Preveza and Vonitsa, the former Venetian mainland ports held by the French

ledger.note: October 1798: Ali seizes Butrint, Igoumenitsa, Preveza and Vonitsa "from the French"; "Parga stayed French". The Ali page: he attacked Preveza in October.

region.text: Himara, raided in 1797 and annexed in 1799, "extending Ali's control along the coast to Vlorë"

ledger.note: 1799: Himara annexed after the 1797 raid in which "more than 6,000 civilians" were killed.

region.text: Delvinë, taken "after seven years of conflict", giving him "Epirus from Arta to Tepelenë and Vlorë"

ledger.note: 1802: Ali takes Delvinë. The Yanina page says he "temporarily subdued" Berat, Delvino and Chameria in 1799 and "reconquered Delvina" in 1811, so the hold was not secure.

region.text: Souli, conquered in 1803 after a siege

ledger.note: 1803: Souli falls; the Ali page says the Souliotes departed and their villages were destroyed after his autumn attack.

region.text: Souli

ledger.note: 1803: the Souliote War ends with the conquest of Souli.

region.text: Karli-Eli (Aetolia-Acarnania), annexed after Mihrişah Valide Sultan's death in 1805

ledger.note: 1806: Ali "finally managed to gain control of Karli-Eli"; invaded in October 1789 but the Ottomans granted it to Mihrişah Valide Sultan, so it was not annexed until 1806.

region.text: the Morea (Peloponnese), as Veli Pasha's Morea Eyalet

ledger.note: 1807: "Veli ruled Morea (Peloponnese), which was incorporated" (1807-1812). Ali page: Veli became Pasha of the Morea Eyalet in 1807.

region.text: Berat, invaded in 1809; its territories passed to Muhtar as a dowry

ledger.note: 1809: Berat falls to Ali's family. The Ali page says the siege is undated (1809-1810) and that Vlorë was conquered afterwards.

region.text: the remainder of the Sanjak of Avlona (Vlorë), after Sephir Bey's assassination

ledger.note: 1810: Ali takes the rest of the Sanjak of Avlona, "stretching his dominion from Durrës in the north to Arta in the south" (Ali page).

region.text: Gjirokastër annexed and Delvina reconquered in 1811; by 1811 "the sanjaks of Ohrid, Elbasan, Gjirokastër and Delvinë were incorporated"

ledger.note: 1811: Gjirokastër "surrendered after a show of force" (Ali page). Ohrid and Elbasan are from the Ali page only; the Mustafa Bushati page gives Ohrid and Elbasan to Scutari in 1824.

region.text: the Morea, which Veli governed from 1807 to 1812

ledger.note: 1812: end of Veli's rule in the Morea ("1807-1812"). The page does not say who took it over.

region.text: Parga, bought from the British and annexed to Delvina

ledger.note: 1819: "Parga acquired from the British and annexed to Delvina"; the inhabitants fled to Corfu. Region was a 60 km circle round Ioannina (land held since 1787); now a 10 km circle on Parga (39.28 N, 20.40 E, from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parga) [reviewer eu-18-x, 2026-11-01].

region.text: "the sanjak of Berat was appropriated to him" (Mustafa Pasha Bushati), in 1820

ledger.note: 1820: Berat goes to Mustafa Pasha Bushati of Scutari; the Mustafa page does not say from whom, and Ali Pasha, declared a rebel in 1820, held Berat since 1809, so the Pashalik of Yanina is the counterpart by the researcher's reading (the pashalik-of-scutari ledger carries the matching gain). [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: added]

region.text: the pashalik's core, Ioannina and Thessaly

ledger.note: 1820: "After being declared a rebel in 1820"; the Yanina page: Mahmud II ordered his deposition, Ali resisted and formed a coalition with the Souliotes on 4 December 1820, with "some 20,000 Turkish troops" against his army. First Ottoman advances are undated on both pages.

region.text: the pashalik

ledger.note: 24 January 1822: Ali Pasha is killed by Ottoman agents and his head sent to the Sultan.

region.text: the pashalik's land

ledger.note: January 1822: Ali Pasha "(1743 - 24 January 1822)"; the pashalik becomes the Ioannina Eyalet.

wars.name: Souliote War
wars.outcome: Ali invaded in 1789 and again in 1790, 1792, 1800 and 1802; peace in 1792 returned captured villages; Souli was conquered in 1803 and the Souliotes left.
wars.note: The Yanina page gives 1789-1803 in one place and 1789-1793 in another.

wars.name: Ottoman campaign against Ali Pasha
wars.outcome: Ali was declared a rebel in 1820, resisted with some 50,000 Albanian troops available to him, and was assassinated on 24 January 1822; the pashalik ended.
wars.note: His Albanian troops left when the Greek revolts broke out in the Morea (Yanina page).

certainty.note: A de facto independent pashalik that "was never officially recognized"; no treaty frontier. Control by appointed sons and sanjak-bey allies was loose on the east and in central Greece.

notes: Cliopatria has no row; all eleven keyframes are new. Disagreements: Yanina page says Delvina was reconquered and Gjirokastër annexed in 1811, Ali page says Delvinë fell in 1802 and the sanjaks were incorporated "by 1811". The 1822 peak list on the Yanina page names the Morea, Elbasan, Ohrid and Görice (Korçë); the Morea is dated 1807-1812 only, Korçë has no date and is left out. Attica: the Ali page says that after the assassination of Selim III in 1808 "Ali occupied Attica by force", the Yanina page says the peak held most of mainland Greece "except Attica"; no end date is given, so it is not in the ledger. Counterparts needing dossiers: pashalik-of-berat (Berat sanjak to 1809), sanjak-of-avlona (Avlona/Vlorë), suliotes (Souli), ioannina-eyalet is the Ottoman successor. Wikidata id null (wikidata.org unreachable). Review fix (2026-11-01): Berat leaves the shape in 1820 (loss to pashalik-of-scutari, confidence 2: the Mustafa page gives the year but not the previous holder, and the page does not mention Ali); the 1812-1822 keyframe is split at 1820. Parga's region was already corrected by the reviewer to a 10 km circle at 20.40 E, 39.28 N. Not done (thin): Attica after 1808 (no end date on the Ali page) and Korçë (undated). Elbasan and Ohrid are in the Yanina shape until 1822 and go to Mustafa in 1824 (Scutari ledger), so 1822-1823 they have no holder in either dossier: the Ottoman Empire's own shape covers them.
